item.title: CSS Circuits: useful quantum circuits that can be simulated with O(1) cost per gate
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Craig Gidney, Cody Jones
arXiv:2611.14944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: "CSS circuits" are quantum circuits generated by X, Z, M_X, M_Z, and CNOT gates. Although CSS circuits are extremely restrictive, they can implement important quantum protocols like teleportation, error correction, and entanglement purification. We present a simple CSS circuit simulator that uses O(1) work per gate. The simulator corresponds to a local hidden variable model, so we use Bell inequalities to prove the simulator can't also support Hadamard gates, CZ gates, or S gates. We note that CSS circuits appear ideal for benchmarking quantum error correction in the presence of atom loss errors.

arXiv:2611.15057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a fundamental quantum sensing task: detecting weak oscillating fields with unknown strength and frequency. Recent work by Allen et al. established a fundamental lower bound on the required sensing time, which they named the "Grover-Heisenberg limit", and gave a protocol attaining this limit. arXiv:2611.15995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Communication scenarios (CS) are arguably the simplest setting in which quantum behaviors can be observed. These depend only on four parameters of the input-output statistics, corresponding to correlated and anticorrelated events. Under dimensional assumptions, saturating one of the inequalities certifies SIC-POVMs with analytical noise robustness.
